  PROBLEM: Bash ANSI-C quoting in a shell `-c` argument is not handled by the nested credential scan, so credentials inside `$'…'` commands can be posted unmasked.
  WHY: `shlex` preserves the leading `$`, preventing credential-command and flag recognition; reviewers differ on severity, with reports ranging from major to blocker.
- .claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py:398, 401; workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py:398, 401 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: `_segment_flag_letters` does not normalize credential-command basenames for case, `.exe` suffixes, or Windows path separators.
  WHY: Credential commands such as `curl.exe` and `MYSQL` can fail to match `_CREDENTIAL_COMMANDS`, leaving credential flag values uncollected and unmasked; reviewers differ on severity, with reports ranging from nit to blocker.
- .claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py:458-460; workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py:458-460 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: `_split_string_runner_before` does not normalize the `env` basename for case, `.exe` suffixes, or Windows path separators.
  WHY: `env -S` nested-command parsing can be skipped for those invocations, leaving credentials in the nested command uncollected and unmasked; reviewers differ on severity, with reports ranging from nit to blocker.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: PR description Finding #1 and Finding #2 — "the credential scan and the shape no longer take the first word as the command" and the round-10 follow-on must apply the basename/case/`.exe` normalisation wherever a runner or credential-command word is matched. Round 10's commit message lists `_shell_runner_before` and the PowerShell cluster rule as the sites it normalised; the credential-command and env-`-S` sites were not in that list, and no new test exercises them.
  expected_change_site: `.claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py` `_split_string_runner_before` (line 460) and `_segment_flag_letters` (lines 398, 401).
  confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  EVIDENCE: The round-10 diff stats `4 files changed, 26 insertions(+), 4 deletions(-)`, and the live `permission_prompts.py` shows `_runner_basename` invoked only at lines 422, 605; lines 398, 401, 460 still use `rsplit("/", 1)[-1]`. The new tests added in round 10 cover only `pwsh.exe` / `powershell.exe` / `/bin/BASH` / `PWSH` / `C:\Tools\pwsh.exe` shells; `tests/test_permission_prompts.py` has no `env.exe` or `curl.exe` case in `test_example_masks_credentials` (line 314+) or `test_shape_never_carries_raw_credentials` (line 589+).
- requirement: Issue #5124 / plan G1: "the values of credential flag values, header values, URL credentials, and credential-named assignments become `***`" for every posted command, including commands that use valid Bash syntax that the current parser does not understand. Bash ANSI-C quoting `$'…'` is valid Bash (the `$'…'` form is referenced in the project's own test fixture `test_credential_free_commands_are_unchanged` and is used by users who need escape sequences inside a `-c` argument).
  expected_change_site: `.claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py` `_backticks_as_substitutions` (line 329) — fold `$'…'` into `$(`/`)` (or strip the `$'` / closing `'` after the existing escape pass) so the recursive `_command_line_credentials` sees a clean command line.
  confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  EVIDENCE: `_backticks_as_substitutions` rewrites only `` ` `` characters (line 361) and escaped backticks (line 348); no `re.match("$'")` or `'` after-`$` handling is present. `tests/test_permission_prompts.py` has no test case with `$'…'` (grep for `$'` in the new test rows returns nothing), and the round-10 commit did not add one.
=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

  PROBLEM: Bash ANSI-C quoting in a shell `-c` argument bypasses the credential scan because `shlex` does not recognize `$'…'` as quoting.
  WHY: The nested command is tokenized with a leading `$`, so credential matching fails and the password can be posted unmasked.

  PROBLEM: `_segment_flag_letters` does not normalize credential-command basenames or strip `.exe` suffixes.
  WHY: Credential flags for `.exe` or differently cased commands may not be detected, leaving passwords unmasked; `_split_string_runner_before` has the same normalization gap for `env`.
  severity=NIT
  confidence=4
